title: CR-Aug: Community Risk-Guided Adaptive Augmentation for Semi-supervised Graph Anomaly Detection

problem.claim: Semi-supervised graph anomaly detection must operate with only a limited number of labeled normal nodes and no real anomaly labels.

gap.claim: Existing uniform anomaly modeling and pseudo-anomaly generation overlook community heterogeneity, producing pseudo-anomalies with limited diversity and specificity.

contributions.claim: CR-Aug is a community risk-guided adaptive augmentation framework for semi-supervised graph anomaly detection.
Community Risk Profiling quantifies community-level risk using the affinity discrepancy between labeled normal nodes and the overall community.
Risk-Guided Synthesis adapts pseudo-anomaly generation using risk-weighted sampling and adaptive mixing.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly present CR-Aug as a novel framework.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that CR-Aug significantly outperforms state-of-the-art semi-supervised graph anomaly detection methods on multiple benchmark datasets.

narrative_sequence.summary: Semi-supervised graph anomaly detection is studied when only limited normal-node supervision is available.
Uniform anomaly modeling and pseudo-anomaly generation ignore community heterogeneity and yield insufficiently diverse and specific pseudo-anomalies.
CR-Aug addresses the limitation through community-specific risk knowledge, using Community Risk Profiling and Risk-Guided Synthesis.
Risk-guided synthesis is intended to produce diverse pseudo-anomalies and more discriminative supervisory signals.
Experiments on multiple benchmark datasets are reported to show significant improvements over state-of-the-art methods.

source_observation.claim: Community heterogeneity is associated with limited diversity and specificity in uniformly generated pseudo-anomalies.

interpretation.claim: Augmentation strategies may benefit from conditioning generation on local or community-level risk differences.

application.claim: For graph anomaly detection with sparse normal supervision, profile community risk and use it to guide pseudo-anomaly sampling and mixing.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether community-risk guidance generalizes beyond the reported benchmark datasets or graph settings.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the benchmark datasets, evaluation metrics, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not describe the implementation details of adaptive mixing or the risk-weighted sampling procedure.
The abstract does not establish independent verification, reproducibility, or performance outside the reported experiments.
